حُبَيْشٌ dim. of حَبَشٌ, q. v. (Msb.) ―
-b2- Also A certain well-known bird; [the Numidia; which comprises the species commonly called the Guineahen, and pintado: so applied in the present day:] the word is thus, [without the article ال, apparently as a proper name, and] in the dim. form, like كُمَيْتٌ and كُعَيْتٌ: (S, TA:) it is strangely omitted in the K. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
